sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The worker has the finitimus type of enteric valve architecture (EVA) and is one of the smallest workers in the genus; the soldier is one of the smallest in the genus (most evident in the comparison of head length): the soldier of I. fungifaber is sometimes equally small, but its enteric valve is of the fungifaber type; the soldier of I. phalloides (also with the finitimus type of enteric valve) may also be this small, but the caecum differs. The alate is unknown.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Coloration: head capsule C4—C5, pale and darkening in long-stored specimens (Cf5—Cf6); gulamentum concolorous with the head capsule; antennae and labrum paler than the head capsule (C3—C4), darkening in long-stored specimens; mandibles dark (C7), the base abruptly one shade paler (C5—C6, concolorous with the frons); thorax, tergites and legs paler than the head capsule (C2—C4), darkening in long-stored specimens; abdomen grey from the gut contents. Setae: head capsule with a few scattered fine setae; a loose tuft of setae on the frons surrounding and hanging over the frontal gland pore (in one specimen very few setae around the frontal gland pore); antennae with conspicuous setae and more numerous small setae, the apical segment with a tuft of very fine curved hairs at its tip (visible above 50×); the labrum always with large setae on the lobes; pronotum and mesonotum with a few setae mainly on the margins; fore coxa with only 1 large seta on the ridge, the trochanter generally with 5—6 setae in a row; fore, mid and hind tibiae with tibial spur formula 3/2/2 and subapical spur formula 0/2/0, each tibia with 4—6 spines in a row; tergites with the large setae mainly on the posterior margin; sternites with long setae (erect or slightly inclined forward, often pigmented) and small setae directed posteriorly. Structure: the soldier is on average distinctly the smallest in the genus, most evident in the comparison of head length. Head capsule distinctly sclerotized, distinctly longer than wide; in dorsal view the sides nearly parallel, slightly convex or narrowing in the posterior 1/3 or 1/4, converging forwards from the antennal sockets towards the mandible bases, the posterior margin rounded; in lateral view distinctly concave, the frons with a low gentle anterior swelling hanging over the frontal gland pore or without a swelling; gulamentum in ventral view narrowing in the posterior half, the anterior half convex at the sides, in lateral view rounded or slightly concave posteriorly; antennae 14.5 or 15 segmented; labrum deeply forked, the sides harp-shaped, the lobes angular or nearly truncate, their tips fine, white or semitransparent, the anterior margin concave; mandibles sabre-like, the inner margin smooth, each with 1 distinct but small marginal tooth (near the molar area), the mandibles distinctly shorter than the head, the surface of both smooth and shining; right mandible slightly more curved than the left; pronotum saddle-shaped, the anterior and posterior margins entire; the fore coxa with a lip-like projection ventrally forming a sharp ridge. Gut: enteric valve inserted on the left side of the abdomen, in the posterior half of the abdomen, best seen in ventral view; enteric valve primary cushions (PC) with trigonal symmetry, the odd cushion slightly longer and slightly wider than the even ones, the crest weakly developed; secondary cushions (SC) broad upstream, distinctly narrowing downstream, the spines evenly distributed; caecum near the middle of the abdomen, best seen in ventral view, with three indistinct lobes. Measurements (Table 19, mm): head dorsal concavity sagitta SHdC 0.01—0.06, head length SHdL 2.35—2.52, head width SHdW 1.74—1.79, left mandible ventral length SMlL 1.55—2.05, left mandible minor curvature SMlc 0.13—0.16.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The original describes the worker here for the first time. Coloration: head capsule pale (C2—C3), turning grey in long-stored specimens; proximal antennal segments pale (C2), the apical segment darker (C3); thorax, tergites and legs pale (C1—C2); abdomen grey to red-brown from the gut contents. Setae: head capsule and postclypeus with a few scattered erect setae; labrum with a few scattered stout setae; antennae with conspicuous setae and more numerous small setae, the apical segment with a tuft of very fine curved hairs at its tip (visible above 50×); tergites with scattered setae; fore coxa ridged, with 1 fine seta, 3—5 spines on the ridge and 0—2 spines ventrally, the trochanter with 6 spines; fore, mid and hind tibiae with tibial spur formula 3/2/2 and subapical spur formula 0/2/0, with 5—6 spines in a row; tergites with scattered setae; sternites with long setae (erect or slightly inclined forward, often pigmented) and small setae directed posteriorly. Structure: the worker is on average one of the smallest in the genus. Head capsule weakly sclerotized (except the mandibles); antennae 14—14.5 segmented; labrum domed, wider than long; left mandible apical tooth well developed, sharp when unworn, with 3 marginal teeth (the first well developed but blunt-tipped, the second weak, expressed as an undulating tooth margin and disappearing with wear, the third blunt-tipped), the proximal premolar generally hidden by the molar prominence, the dorsal surface of the molar with a rounded prominence ending posteriorly in a small sharp process; right mandible apical tooth well developed, sharp when unworn, with 2 marginal teeth, the molar with a rounded labial process ventrally and heel-shaped posteriorly; pronotum saddle-shaped; the fore coxa with a lip-like projection ventrally forming a sharp ridge. Gut: enteric valve inserted on the left side of the abdomen, in the posterior half of the abdomen, best seen in ventral view; enteric valve primary cushions of the finitimus type with trigonal symmetry, the downstream part of the odd cushion broad, densely covered with rather short setae on a bulbous inflation, with 22—33 supporting setae on each side; secondary cushions broad upstream, distinctly narrowing downstream, the spines evenly distributed; caecum small, near the middle of the abdomen, visible in ventral view, the lobes short (small, sometimes only faintly outlined). Measurements (Table 19, mm): maximum head width WHdW 1.06—1.08, distance from the left mandible apical tooth to the first marginal tooth WMlAmD 0.16—0.19, left mandible functional length WMlL 0.51—0.54; mean length of enteric valve primary cushions 0.55—0.58, width 0.06—0.08, mean length of secondary cushions 0.43—0.46, width 0.22—0.24, odd primary cushion elongation index 7.36—9.61.

note: Adapted from the genus revision in Josens et al. (2025), original in English; the alate is unknown in the original; the worker is described here for the first time; measurements from Table 19 and the text of the original; the original places this species in the chapter Incertae sedis - species inquirenda and notes that it may be a synonym of I. bulbifrons based on young colonies; distribution, hosts, DNA and figure numbers are not translated.
